His saying ﴿And forsake them with graceful forsaking﴾ guides His Messenger to abandon the Quraysh disbelievers and not to confront them; graceful forsaking is that which contains no reproach. His saying ﴿And leave Me with the deniers, possessors of luxury﴾, that is, leave Me with the deniers, the chieftains of Quraysh, the possessors of luxury, meaning the blessings and affluence. ﴿And give them respite a little﴾, that is, wait for them and do not hasten, for I will suffice you against them. Not much time passed before they were destroyed at Badr at the hands of the believers. And His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire and food that chokes﴾, that is, with Us in the Hereafter are shackles, iron fetters, and a blazing, burning Fire, and a painful punishment, that is, a painful, agonizing one. And food that is the zaqqum and the dari', which chokes the one who eats it in his throat. And a painful punishment, that is, agonizing, which happens to its people and befalls them on a Day when the earth and the mountains quake, that is, move and convulse, and the mountains will be a heap of sand, collapsing after having been gathered. And His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, We have sent to you﴾, that is, O people of Makkah and all those beyond them of the rest of mankind and the jinn, ﴿a Messenger as a witness over you﴾ concerning what you do in this world, so that you may be recompensed for it in the Hereafter. And His saying ﴿as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾, that is, Musa son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, ﴿but Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a heavy seizing﴾, that is, a severe, harsh one. And His saying, Exalted is He, addressing the disbelieving deniers: ﴿Then how will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day﴾, that is, the punishment of a Day ﴿which will make the children grey-haired﴾, and that is because of its terror and the distress that befalls, and it is enough that ﴿the sky will be split open by it﴾, that is, cleft because of its terrors.

And that is the Day on which the Lord, Exalted is He, will say to Adam: "O Adam, send forth the group of the Fire." That is, take from every thousand of the people of the place of standing nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire, and not one out of every thousand will be saved. Here the trial intensifies and the distress becomes great. His saying ﴿His promise is always fulfilled﴾, that is, His promise, Exalted is He, of the coming of this Day is fulfilled, meaning it is certainly going to happen. His saying ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder﴾, that is, indeed these verses containing the mention of the Resurrection and its terrors are a reminder, admonition and lesson. ﴿So whoever wills takes to his Lord a path﴾, so let him take it, and it is faith and righteous deeds after abandoning polytheism and sins.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The obligation of patience in obedience and in refraining from disobedience.
2. Graceful forsaking is that which contains no reproach.
3. Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood.
4. Affirmation of resurrection and recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 73, verse 20:

Explanation of the words:

"Anna taqum" (that you stand): i.e., for the tahajjud (night prayer).

"Adna" (less than): i.e., fewer.

"Wa ta'ifatun" (and a group): i.e., a group with you from your companions also stands likewise.

"Wallahu yuqaddiru al-layla wa al-nahar" (And Allah measures the night and the day): i.e., He counts them and knows what has passed of the hours of each of them and what remains.

"Alima an lan tuhsuhu" (He knows that you will not be able to count it): i.e., the night, so you cannot keep up its standing all of it, because that would be hard upon you.

"Fa-taba 'alaykum" (so He turned to you): i.e., He returned you to lightening the standing in the night, since that is the original ruling.

"Fa-iqra'u ma tayassara" (So recite what is easy of it): i.e., pray in the night what is easy for you, even two rak'ahs.

"Wa aqimu al-salah" (And establish the prayer): i.e., the obligatory prayer.

"Wa atu al-zakah" (And give the zakah): i.e., the obligatory zakah.

"Wa aqridu Allaha qardan hasanan" (And lend to Allah a goodly loan): i.e., give charity from the surplus of your wealth, with your souls content with it; that is the goodly loan.

"Wa ma tuqaddimu li-anfusikum min khayr" (And whatever good you send forward for yourselves): i.e., from voluntary acts of worship, such as prayer, charity, fasting, hajj and others.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted informs His Messenger that He knows what he and a group of his companions stand in the night, and that they sometimes stand for less than two-thirds of the night, i.e., less, and sometimes for half and a third, as at the beginning of the surah. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] almost two-thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you﴾. And His saying ﴿And Allah measures the night and the day﴾, i.e., He counts their hours, so He knows what has passed of the night and what remains of its hours. And His saying ﴿He knows that you will not be able to count it﴾, i.e., you will not be able to keep track of its hours, so standing for most of it is hard upon you, though you intended what was required. ﴿So He turned to you﴾ in that regard. By this, the obligatory night standing was abrogated, and the recommended remained, performed even with two rak'ahs in any part of the night, though performing them after the 'Isha' prayer is more excellent. His saying ﴿So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾, i.e., pray what is easy of the night. He used the word "Qur'an" while meaning prayer, because the Qur'an is the principal part of the night prayer. His saying ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others who travel through the land seeking of Allah's bounty, and others who fight in the cause of Allah﴾: here He mentions three excuses for them, namely illness, travel through the land for trade, and jihad in the cause of Allah, all of which make night standing difficult. Out of mercy for the believers, Allah abrogated this burdensome ruling with His saying ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾, repeating it to emphasize the abrogation of the night standing that had been obligatory and, by this verse, became recommended. His saying "And establish the prayer and give the zakah" means the obligatory ones. His saying "And lend to Allah a goodly loan" means spend in the cause of Allah, which is jihad, for the good deed in it is multiplied to seven hundred. "And whatever good you send forward for yourselves" refers to voluntary prayers, charities, hajj and all other acts of worship; you will find it with Allah on the Day of Resurrection as better and greater in reward. His saying "And seek forgiveness from Allah" concerns every shortcoming that comes from you in regard to the rights of Allah the Exalted. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful: He forgives whoever repents and has mercy on him, so He does not hold him to account for a sin he has repented of.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification of what the Messenger ﷺ and his companions used to stand in the night for, in tahajjud.

2- Abrogation of the obligation of night standing, and the remaining of its recommendation and encouragement.

3- The obligation of establishing the prayer and giving the zakah.

4- Encouragement toward voluntary acts of worship in general.

5- The obligation of seeking forgiveness upon sin, and its recommendation and desirability at all times, because of the shortcomings that occur.
